ground_truth.description: BaseAuth.recoverSapientSignature returns bytes32(uint256(1)) instead of actual signer imageHash, violating ISapient interface. Breaks Merkle leaf construction in BaseSig.recoverBranch.
ground_truth.root_cause: BaseAuth.recoverSapientSignature returns bytes32(uint256(1)) instead of actual signer imageHash, violating ISapient interface. Breaks Merkle leaf construction in BaseSig.recoverBranch.
ground_truth.attack_scenario: Wallet uses another wallet as sapient signer → signature validation fails due to incorrect image hash. PoC: Add test to test/modules/BaseSig.t.sol: test_BaseAuth_recoverSapientSignature_ReturnsConstant. Deploys MinimalSapient, crafts signature, asserts constant return.
ground_truth.fix_description: Return actual image hash from recoverSapientSignature. Extend signatureValidation to return imageHash or call BaseSig.recover.

vulnerabilities.explanation: The function recoverSapientSignature returns a constant bytes32(uint256(1)) instead of the actual signer image hash, violating the ISapient interface. This breaks the Merkle leaf construction in BaseSig.recoverBranch.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: A wallet using another wallet as a sapient signer will fail signature validation due to the incorrect image hash being returned. This can lead to unintended behavior or failure in signature verification processes that rely on the correct image hash.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Return the actual image hash from recoverSapientSignature. This can be achieved by modifying the function to correctly compute and return the image hash instead of the constant value.

prediction.overall_explanation: The BaseAuth contract contains a logic error in the recoverSapientSignature function, which returns a constant value instead of the actual image hash. This violates the ISapient interface and can cause issues with signature validation and Merkle leaf construction. The contract is considered vulnerable due to this logic error.
